application.name: ofetch
application.summary: The codebase implements a reusable fetch wrapper. Its central factory builds a $fetch client that merges options, constructs URLs, serializes request bodies, performs fetches, parses responses by content type, invokes hooks, retries selected failures, and throws normalized errors. Supporting modules handle URL/query utilities, option/header merging, response-type detection, and error creation.
application.purpose: A TypeScript HTTP client library that wraps the Fetch API and provides a typed $fetch helper with request defaults, URL/query construction, automatic body serialization, response parsing, lifecycle hooks, retries, timeouts, and normalized FetchError handling.

applicationFacts: The public API is built around $fetch, $fetch.raw, $fetch.native, and $fetch.create.
$fetch returns parsed response data, while $fetch.raw returns the full FetchResponse object including _data.
createFetch accepts global defaults and a custom fetch implementation, and supports creating derived clients with merged default options.
Request URLs can be modified with baseURL and query/params merging.
JSON-serializable bodies are automatically stringified and default Content-Type/Accept headers are set to application/json.
FormData, URLSearchParams, streams, buffers, and similar non-JSON payloads are handled separately from automatic JSON serialization.
Response parsing is selected from responseType or inferred from the Content-Type header, supporting json, text, blob, arrayBuffer, and stream.
Timeouts are implemented with AbortSignal.timeout and AbortSignal.any.
Retries can be configured by count, delay, and status-code list; default retry status codes include 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504.
Lifecycle hooks include onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, and onResponseError.
Errors are normalized into FetchError instances that expose request, options, response, data, status, statusCode, statusText, and statusMessage accessors.
The test suite runs against a local H3 server with routes covering normal responses, URL/query handling, body echoing, binary content, 403/408/404 errors, 204 no-content, and timeouts.
The examples demonstrate typed consumption of JSON HTTP responses.
